title: Parametric optimization of lead-free CsSnI 3 -based perovskite solar cells for enhanced photovoltaic efficiency
content: Growing concerns regarding planetary energy instability and the erosion of environmental integrity have significantly promoted the advancements of renewable energy solutions, with solar power leading the shift toward a cleaner, greener future. Among solar cell technologies, the low production cost and outstanding photovoltaic efficiency of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have fueled their exponential rise within the domain of clean energy studies. In this work, lead-free ZnO/CsSnI3/Spiro-OMeTAD PSCs were systematically investigated through 1D COMSOL simulations, employing CsSnI3 as a non-toxic and highly stable perovskite absorber. A maximum fill factor (FF) of 81.53% is achieved, corresponding to an optimized power conversion (PCE) of 21.53% at an optimal device temperature of 250 K. A maximum short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 29.202 mA cm−2 is achieved when the acceptor density is set to NA = 1 × 1018 cm−3, while the maximum power output (Pmax) attains 215.376 W m−2 at 250 K. Device performance is systematically optimized by varying key physical and structural parameters, including the thickness of individual layers, operating temperature, and carrier concentration densities. The attainment of a PCE of 21.53% positions this work as a meaningful contribution toward high-performance lead-free photovoltaic technologies, supporting the broader transition to sustainable and eco-friendly energy systems.
